title: AI Search and Vector Search
description: Learn how Azure AI Search adds full-text search, vector search, semantic ranking, and skillsets to help users find information across documents.

data.text: Azure AI Search is a cloud search service that adds fast, relevant search over structured and unstructured data. You can connect it to documents in Blob Storage, SQL Database, Cosmos DB, or other sources. The service indexes the content so users can search with keywords, filters, and even natural language. Newer features like vector search and semantic ranking make it useful for AI-powered applications that need to understand meaning, not just matching words.

data.title: What Azure AI Search Can Do
items: Full-text search with language-specific analyzers and tokenization.
Vector search using embeddings from Azure OpenAI or other models.
Semantic ranking that reorders results by conceptual relevance.
Skillsets that enrich data during indexing using built-in or custom skills.
Faceted navigation, filters, and autocomplete for polished search experiences.

data.content: Send a PUT request to create a simple index for documents with title, content, and a vector field.

data.text: Skillsets let you transform raw data into richer search content during indexing. Built-in skills can extract text from images, detect the language of a document, split text into chunks for embeddings, or call an Azure OpenAI model to generate a vector. Custom skills let you run your own code, such as calling an external API or applying proprietary business logic. Skillsets run inside the indexer and write enriched fields back to the index.

terms.definition: A crawler that pulls data from a data source, applies a skillset, and stores results in a search index.
A collection of enrichment steps that an indexer runs to transform raw data into searchable fields.
A search mode that compares numerical vector embeddings to find results with similar meaning.
A ranking layer that uses machine learning to reorder search results by conceptual relevance rather than keyword match alone.

data.text: Traditional keyword search works well when users know exact terms. Vector search is better when users describe what they need in natural language or when the same concept is expressed in many different ways. For example, a user searching for ways to reduce cloud costs might not use the exact phrase 'cost optimization,' but a semantic search engine can still return relevant results.

data.title: Create and Query an Azure AI Search Index
data.description: Provision an Azure AI Search service, create an index with a vector field, upload sample documents, and run a semantic search query.
steps: Create an Azure AI Search service in the Azure portal.
Create a data source connected to a sample JSON file or Azure Blob Storage.
Create a skillset that generates vectors using the built-in Azure Open AI skill.
Create an index with a vector field and semantic configuration.
Create and run an indexer to populate the index.
Query the index using the search explorer or a REST client.
data.expectedOutcome: You can define a vector-enabled search index, run an indexer with a skillset, and retrieve semantically ranked search results.

data.title: Azure AI Search at a Glance
points: Azure AI Search adds fast, relevant search over documents stored in Azure.
Vector search and semantic ranking help users find results by meaning, not just exact keywords.
Skillsets enrich raw documents during indexing with built-in or custom logic.
Indexers automate the process of connecting data sources, enriching content, and populating the search index.
data.takeaway: Azure AI Search turns raw documents into a discoverable knowledge base that understands both keywords and natural language meaning.
